title: Change-of-Pace Lane Lines
description: Players alternate between a slow, controlled dribble and a sudden burst between the lines, learning that speed change beats a defender as well as a move does.

content.objective: Use a slow-to-fast change of pace, with no change of hand, to gain a step on a defender.
content.setup: Three lines on the baseline (left, middle, right), a ball each.
content.organization: First player in each line goes together; next group leaves at the free-throw line.
instructions: Jog with a high control dribble to the free-throw line extended.
Sprint with a low, pushed dribble to the half-court line.
Hesitate: slow down, rise up slightly, keep dribbling.
Burst again to the far free-throw line and finish at the rim.
Come back on the other side using the other hand.
coachingPoints: The slow phase is a weapon: look relaxed, then explode.
Push the ball out in front on the burst.
Lower the hips the instant you speed up.
commonMistakes: One steady speed the whole length.
Sprinting with the ball behind the hip.
Hesitation so long the dribble dies.
content.safety: Lines stay in their own third of the court; finishers clear the lane straight away.
progressions: Add a trailing defender who starts one metre behind.
Combine each burst with a crossover.
regressions: Shorten the run to half court.
variations: The coach calls 'slow' or 'go' at random.
Finish with a pull-up instead of a lay-up.
successCriteria: Clear difference between the slow and fast phases.
Ball kept in front of the body on every burst.
content.gameApplication: Most open lanes come from a change of speed: the defender relaxes, and the ball handler goes.
